strengths: Mathematically rigorous derivation of the exact solution for diffusion SDEs (Proposition 4.1) using sophisticated techniques (Dubins-Schwarz theorem, exponential integrators)
Clever use of Brownian intervals to avoid storing the entire Wiener process trajectory, addressing a genuine practical concern
Well-motivated problem formulation: Section 3 clearly articulates truncation errors and stability issues with naive SDE inversion
Elegant theoretical framework using Fisk-Stratonovich integrals to achieve time symmetry in the solver
Sound mathematical presentation with detailed proofs in appendices
weaknesses: Severely limited experimental validation: only one proof-of-concept experiment (image interpolation with 20 steps), purely qualitative results, no quantitative metrics (LPIPS, reconstruction error, timing), no comparison with recent competing methods (EDICT, BELM, BELM-image)
Critical unrealistic assumption that data prediction model is trained to zero loss (xˆ₀|ₜ = x₀|ₜ); robustness to imperfect score functions never analyzed
Incomplete algorithm specification: the single-step solver Ψₕ for the exponential integral is never defined or explained; Taylor approximation error analysis is absent
Misleading 'exact inversion' claim when the exponential integral is approximated; the truncation error from this approximation is not quantified
Missing stability analysis despite being central motivation: no quantitative validation of claimed stability improvements over baselines

Limited technical novelty: heavily adapts reversible solver framework from McCallum & Foster (2024); exponential integrators for diffusion are established; main contribution is an implementation technique rather than algorithmic advance
No ablation studies or sensitivity analysis: coupling parameter ζ=0.999 chosen without justification; no study of sensitivity to number of steps, different models, or score function quality
Reproducibility concerns: critical implementation details missing (Ψₕ specification, Brownian interval computation efficiency), code not provided, minimal experimental details
Missing demonstrations of stated applications: image editing and guided generation via continuous adjoint equations are mentioned but never demonstrated
No computational cost analysis: timing comparisons, memory overhead of augmented state xˆ, and scalability to larger models/images not evaluated

strengths: Solid theoretical foundation: Proposition 4.1 provides a mathematically rigorous exact solution decomposition using variation of parameters, exponential integrators, and the Dubins-Schwarz theorem
Well-motivated problem: Clear articulation of truncation error and stability issues in existing forward/backward diffusion inversion methods
Sophisticated mathematical machinery: Effective use of Stratonovich integrals, exponential integrators, and Brownian interval techniques
Claim of memory efficiency without storing entire Wiener process is novel if substantiated
weaknesses: Critically insufficient experimental validation: Only one qualitative image interpolation example with no quantitative metrics, ablations, or comparisons—far below ICML standards for claims of exact inversion and efficiency

Central claims inadequately justified: (1) 'Exact inversion without storing Wiener process' unclear—equations still reference W_ςn increments without explaining how Brownian intervals avoid path storage; (2) 'Algebraically reversible' not empirically validated—no encode→decode recovery tests; (3) ζ=0.999 suggests possible numerical sensitivity

Limited novelty: Primarily combines existing techniques (McCallum & Foster 2024 coupling, standard exponential integrators, existing Brownian intervals). Distinction from Wu & De la Torre (2022) unconvincing

Incomplete technical exposition: Ψ_h solver unspecified, Stratonovich expansion order barely mentioned, zero-loss model assumption unrealistic and undiscussed, Brownian interval mechanism delegated to citations without explanation
No comparison with recent exact inversion methods: EDICT, BELM, Wang et al. (2024) mentioned but not quantitatively compared despite being central related work

Missing critical ablations and analysis: No evaluation of ζ sensitivity, approximation order effects, truncation errors, timing/memory profiling, stability regions, or robustness to model imperfection

Experimental design issues: Artificially low step count (20 steps) to 'stress test,' qualitative-only evaluation inadequate for validation, task choice (interpolation) too benign, claimed application (guided generation) not evaluated
Reproducibility concerns: Missing implementation details (solver specification, hyperparameters), no code release mentioned, no discussion of handling nonzero model training error

strengths: Solid mathematical framework with rigorous derivation of exact SDE solution (Proposition 4.1), elegantly decomposing the problem into linear, approximated, and Brownian bridge terms
Novel technical contribution: first method for exact SDE inversion without storing the entire Wiener process, using efficient Brownian interval representation
Well-motivated problem statement in Section 3, clearly articulating real issues (truncation error misalignment and bidirectional numerical stability) with naive forward-time inversion
Clever algorithmic contribution adapting recent reversible ODE solver techniques (McCallum & Foster, 2024) to the SDE setting with coupling parameter approach
Generally clear presentation of mathematical derivations and logical flow from theory to practical solver implementation
weaknesses: Severely insufficient experimental validation: only a single qualitative image interpolation experiment on 256×256 CelebA-HQ images with no quantitative metrics (PSNR, LPIPS, FID) or statistical testing, falling far short of ICML standards
No computational cost analysis despite memory efficiency being a key claimed benefit—memory usage, runtime, and step count comparisons entirely absent
Missing critical comparison with Wu & De la Torre (2022), the most directly related SDE inversion work; practical advantages over their method remain unclear
Unverified stability claims: motivation emphasizes bidirectional stability but no empirical demonstration of forward/backward error behavior or error magnification analysis
Approximation error not analyzed: no study of how truncation errors from Taylor expansion accumulate, no comparison of expansion orders, no error scaling analysis with step count
Critical assumption of zero-loss trained models not addressed: no sensitivity analysis for imperfect models or guidance on real-world applicability
Coupling parameter ζ used without justification or ablation study; no analysis of its effect on stability or practical guidance for practitioners
Severely limited experimental scope: no image editing or guided generation experiments despite these being primary motivating applications; only single modality, single task, single resolution tested
Reproducibility concerns: no code availability, minimal implementation details, cannot verify 'exact inversion' claims without quantitative results
Notation clarity issue: footnote acknowledging different Wiener processes between equations is confusing and should be clarified in main text

strengths: Novel theoretical contribution: Exact SDE inversion without storing entire Brownian motion trajectories, achieved through systematic framework combining exponential Runge-Kutta methods and Lawson methods
Rigorous mathematical framework: Well-founded convergence proofs (Theorems 4.1-4.2) with formal propositions for ODE/SDE time reparameterization and complete proofs in appendices

Comprehensive experimental validation: Covers unconditional generation (DDPM), conditional generation (Stable Diffusion), and interpolation with quantitative metrics (FID, CLIP, Image Reward) and multiple baselines
Systematic connections to prior work: Elegantly shows how existing solvers (DPM-Solver variants, DDIM) emerge as special cases, with detailed comparison table of solver properties
Strong implementation support: Detailed derivations, closed-form inverse functions for noise schedules, specific Runge-Kutta tableaux, and guidance for reproducibility
Honest treatment of fundamental limitations: Candidly discusses stability constraints and tradeoffs rather than overselling capabilities
weaknesses: Stability severely limits applicability: All reversible methods have poor/absent linear stability regions, restricting step sizes and reducing theoretical convergence order advantages in practice (acknowledged in Appendix A.2 but not sufficiently emphasized)

Marginal practical improvements: Experimental results show competitive but not dramatically superior performance; many applications don't require exact reversibility, limiting practical motivation for adopting complex methods

Brownian motion reconstruction benefits unclear: Virtual Brownian Tree and related techniques add algorithmic complexity, but actual memory and computational overhead vs. full trajectory storage is never quantified with real numbers
Missing computational cost analysis: No wall-clock time or memory comparisons provided; practical efficiency matters as much as theoretical properties for practitioners

Dense presentation limiting accessibility: Heavy notation and mathematical exposition in main paper; key insights and limitations scattered or relegated to appendices; intuition for why reversibility matters in practice could be better motivated

Limited experimental scope: Restricted to small-to-medium images (≤512×512); data prediction formulation fails in certain settings (Figure 9); convergence order advantages don't materialize empirically in small-step regimes (Table 2)

Incremental novelty: Core reversible solver idea dates to 1950s-1980s; the SDE extension without full trajectory storage is valuable but somewhat specialized, building systematically on rather than fundamentally advancing prior work

Gap between theory and practice: Theory requires space-time Lévy area for strong convergence, but practical implementations often omit it; assumptions like σ_T > 0 for noise prediction models not universally satisfied
